title: Job offer, user decides
spec: User brings detailed personal context about a job offer. AI lays out considerations and asks questions. User weighs them and makes their own decision. Nothing is built.

messages.content: I got an offer from a startup in Oslo: 620k NOK, 0.3% equity, fully remote allowed. My current job in Trondheim pays 680k, stable, but I've stopped learning. I have a mortgage and no kids. Should I take it?

A few things to weigh:

- Money: you'd take a 60k cut. With a mortgage, check whether your monthly margin still feels comfortable if the startup misses payroll for a month.
- Equity: 0.3% only matters if the company has a large exit. Ask about the latest valuation and the vesting schedule.
- Learning: you say you've stopped learning, which tends to matter more over five years than a 9% salary difference.
- Risk: startups fail often; how long could you job-hunt on savings?

Two questions: how many months of expenses do you have saved, and what specifically would you learn there?
About 8 months saved. I'd be the second data engineer, so I'd own the whole pipeline, which I've never done. I think the learning matters most to me. But 60k less hurts.

Eight months of runway is a solid cushion, and owning a pipeline end to end is exactly the kind of experience that's hard to get in a stable company. The salary gap is the main cost. Many startups have some room on base salary when the candidate has a competing reason to stay.
OK, here's my decision: I'll ask them for 660k. If they meet it or come close, I'll take it. If not, I stay and look for a new internal team instead.
That's a clear plan with a sensible fallback. Good luck with the negotiation.
